title: Shrinking finite unramified pieces to disjoint clopen closed immersions
statement: Let $f:X\to S$ be separated [def-weil-proper-morphism], $g:U\to S$ any morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme], and $u\in U$. Fix $n\ge0$, $x:\{0,\ldots,n-1\}\to X$, integers $m_i\ge0$, opens $V_a\subseteq X\times_SU$ [def-pc-fibre-product, def-weil-open-immersion] indexed by $a=(i,j)$ with $j<m_i$, and points $v_a\in V_a$. Suppose each $\pi_a:V_a\to U$ is finite [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism] and unramified [def-weil-unramified-morphism], has unique point $v_a$ over $u$, and has purely inseparable residue extension $\kappa(\pi_a(v_a))\to\kappa(v_a)$ [def-weil-residue-field, def-weil-pbc-finite-purely-inseparable-extension]. Assume the marked points are pairwise distinct in the pullback and every point over $u$ mapping to a listed $x_i$ is one of them. There is an open $B\subseteq U$ containing $u$ and opens $V'_a\subseteq X\times_SB$, with the same index set, which are closed and pairwise disjoint. Each $V'_a\to B$ is a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion] whose image contains the point $u_B=(u\in B)$. Every point of $X\times_SB$ over $u_B$ mapping to a listed $x_i$ lies in some $V'_a$. No remainder or covering decomposition is asserted.

source.place: Tag 04DG (lemma-finite-unramified-one-point), then Tag 04HI (lemma-unramified-etale-local-technical), the pairwise-intersection deletion argument; Tag 01W6 for proper-over-separated

proof.text: Apply the finite unramified one-point closed-immersion theorem to every piece. Since each piece is finite over U and the projection to U is separated, IsProper.of_comp makes its open inclusion proper, hence its image is closed.

Intersect the finitely many neighbourhoods supplied for the pieces. For each pair of distinct indices, the intersection is closed in the first finite piece, so its image in U is closed. Uniqueness of the marked fibre points and injectivity show that every such image avoids u. Remove these images and base change the family to the remaining open B.

The pullback of each piece is the preimage open. Pullback pasting identifies its morphism to B with a further restriction of the closed immersion over its chosen neighbourhood, so it remains a closed immersion. The deleted pairwise images make the pieces pairwise disjoint, and pullback along B preserves the marked points and the stated exhaustion.

theorem exists_disjoint_closed_immersion_refinement
    {X S U : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) [IsSeparated f] (g : U ⟶ S) (u : U)
    (n : ℕ) (x : Fin n → X) (m : Fin n → ℕ)
    (V : (Σ i : Fin n, Fin (m i)) → (pullback f g).Opens)
    (v : (a : Σ i : Fin n, Fin (m i)) → (V a).toScheme)
    (hpieces : ∀ a, IsFinite ((V a).ι ≫ pullback.snd f g) ∧
      (LocallyOfFiniteType ((V a).ι ≫ pullback.snd f g) ∧
        IsOpenImmersion (pullback.diagonal ((V a).ι ≫ pullback.snd f g))) ∧
      ((V a).ι ≫ pullback.snd f g) (v a) = u ∧
      (∀ w : (V a).toScheme, ((V a).ι ≫ pullback.snd f g) w = u → w = v a) ∧
      (letI : Algebra (U.residueField (((V a).ι ≫ pullback.snd f g) (v a)))
          ((V a).toScheme.residueField (v a)) :=
        (((V a).ι ≫ pullback.snd f g).residueFieldMap (v a)).hom.toAlgebra
       IsPurelyInseparable (U.residueField (((V a).ι ≫ pullback.snd f g) (v a)))
         ((V a).toScheme.residueField (v a))))
    (hinjective : Function.Injective (fun a ↦ (V a).ι (v a)))
    (hexhaust : ∀ (i : Fin n) (p : ↥(pullback f g)),
      (pullback.snd f g).base p = u → (pullback.fst f g).base p = x i →
        ∃ a, p = (V a).ι (v a)) :
    ∃ (B : U.Opens) (huB : u ∈ B),
      ∃ V' : (Σ i : Fin n, Fin (m i)) → (pullback f (B.ι ≫ g)).Opens,
        (∀ a, IsClosed (V' a : Set ↥(pullback f (B.ι ≫ g)))) ∧
        Pairwise (fun a b ↦ Disjoint (V' a) (V' b)) ∧
        (∀ a, IsClosedImmersion ((V' a).ι ≫ pullback.snd f (B.ι ≫ g)) ∧
          (⟨u, huB⟩ : B.toScheme) ∈
            Set.range (((V' a).ι ≫ pullback.snd f (B.ι ≫ g)).base)) ∧
        (∀ (i : Fin n) (p : ↥(pullback f (B.ι ≫ g))),
          (pullback.snd f (B.ι ≫ g)).base p = (⟨u, huB⟩ : B.toScheme) →
          (pullback.fst f (B.ι ≫ g)).base p = x i → ∃ a, p ∈ V' a)
